notes: This registry is hand-maintained and intentionally opinionated.
Status and pressure are review judgments, not automatic scores.
The current center of gravity is continuity/workflow first, then weird/generative deepening.
Refresh it after meaningful implementation or doctrine shifts so the machine-room view stays trustworthy.
drift-review now gives extracted drift its own bounded review surface, keeping the weird line inspectable without bloating extraction.
field-notes now gives lived observation, atmosphere, and recurring motifs their own bounded archive surface instead of dissolving them into general notes.

projects.name: workbench
projects.what_it_does: Collects residue, indexes the archive/foundry, supports review, digest, query, and promotion into real artifacts.
notes: This is still the continuity center of the current foundry.
The weak-residue review and handling policy now exist as explicit notes rather than only open irritation.
Several nearby tools depend on its capture, review, digest, and promotion state staying legible.
next_actions: Operationalize the continuity doctrine and memory-promotion practice through ordinary use rather than more abstract planning.
Only add weak-residue helper behavior if review surfaces still feel noisy after the new policy is lived a bit.
Keep the scope legible so Workbench does not collapse into a management system.
signals: Continuity layering, memory promotion, and weak-residue policy are now explicit parts of the substrate around it.
Artifact-health, resurfacer, orbit-map, and capture-audit still lean on Workbench state.

projects.name: drift-extractor
projects.what_it_does: Extracts unresolved questions, tensions, and unfinished edges from markdown so they can become new captures or artifacts.
notes: Accepted and elevated as the strongest weird/generative candidate in the toolset.
A concrete integration plan now exists, recurrence structures give its outputs a more meaningful downstream home, and drift-review now provides the first bounded review companion.
The next move should remain narrow: use the new review surface before deciding on further deepening.
next_actions: Use drift-review in actual review passes and note what still feels missing before dispatching another slice.
Keep extraction heuristic and inspectable; avoid summary mode, heavy state, or opaque scoring creep.
Let recurrence usage teach what downstream shape is needed before adding more export or ontology machinery.
signals: Decision state still marks it as a main weird/generative center of gravity.
Drift-extractor integration plan, continuity recurrence notes, and drift-review now exist as concrete framing and review artifacts.

projects.name: drift-review
projects.what_it_does: Provides a terminal-first review surface for drift-extracted captures, grouping by source and separating stronger extracted pressure from weak extraction residue.
dependencies: source markdown artifacts for excerpt context
notes: This is the first downstream review companion for drift-extractor rather than an expansion of extraction itself.
Its value is in making extracted pressure inspectable in context while hiding weak extraction residue by default.
It should remain a bounded review surface, not a generalized meaning engine.
next_actions: Use it during real drift review to see whether the current source-grouped surface is enough or whether one more narrow helper is actually needed.
Keep the classification heuristic inspectable and presentation-level.
Only deepen it if lived recurrence review exposes a concrete missing move.
signals: The drift integration plan now has a first concrete implementation step behind it.
This tool helps test whether recurrence-facing review can stay small and useful.

projects.name: artifact-health
projects.what_it_does: Diagnoses structural health in the artifact ecosystem using the Workbench index, separating content-health failures from broader archive roughness.
notes: Accepted after the interpretation and balancing passes; it is good enough to pause.
Its current shape separates content-health failures from broader archive roughness in a useful way.
Best treated as a diagnostic surface, not a truth machine or architecture driver.
next_actions: Leave it quiet unless real archive review reveals a concrete tuning need.
If revisited later, treat the work as taste-balancing rather than rescue or expansion.
signals: Settled state says the balancing pass was accepted as-is and future work should be tuning, not rescue.

projects.name: capture-audit
projects.what_it_does: Audits Workbench captures and review state to surface weak residue, duplicate-ish entries, suspiciously short captures, and review pressure.
notes: Accepted as-is as the first successful runner-built utility.
Its heuristics remain presentation-only and deliberately coarse.
The policy questions it surfaced have now turned into explicit review and handling notes.
next_actions: Keep using it as a support surface during archive review rather than expanding it preemptively.
Only revisit the tool if lived weak-residue handling exposes a concrete default-view problem that simple policy alone does not solve.
signals: Weak residue review and weak residue handling policy now exist, lowering pressure on the tool itself.

projects.name: postsmith
projects.what_it_does: Scaffolds and validates blog posts/pages so other foundry tools can hand work into the public writing archive cleanly.
notes: This is a foundation project rather than the current frontier.
Workbench promotion already uses it as a handoff target.
It matters because several workflows assume a boring, reliable scaffold layer exists.
next_actions: Leave it mostly alone unless promotion workflows expose a concrete gap.
Keep compatibility with the current blog layout explicit if the blog evolves.
signals: Workbench and blog artifact creation depend on it behaving predictably.

projects.name: resurfacer
projects.what_it_does: Surfaces older artifacts from the blog and foundry using simple temporal and theme-based heuristics so recurrence stays visible.
notes: It already does the core job in a small inspectable way.
It sits near the new creative-recurrence line, but the recurrence structures are notes-first for now rather than tool pressure.
It remains part of the continuity ecosystem without being the current bottleneck.
next_actions: Let it sit unless real archive growth or recurrence practice reveals a concrete tuning need.
If recurrence or drift integration touches it later, do so through a bounded plan rather than folding tools together wholesale.
signals: Creative recurrence structures now exist as a note-level experiment, which clarifies that resurfacer does not need to absorb that role yet.

projects.name: bootstrapper
projects.what_it_does: Scaffolds new foundry projects with a README, design note, and optional starter script so new experiments begin with clean local structure.
notes: Useful machine-room hygiene tool.
Its job is straightforward and currently complete enough.
next_actions: Use it when spinning up new experiments; otherwise leave it alone.
signals: No active pressure is visible around scaffolding right now.

projects.name: dispatch-template
projects.what_it_does: Prints a reusable bounded execution-brief scaffold for implementation dispatches to runner or future execution lanes.
notes: This is a small support tool for the machine-room staffing pattern.
It is intentionally a printer of structure, not a dispatch system.
next_actions: Keep it small and reusable; do not let it grow into orchestration logic.
signals: The multi-agent loop exists now, but the template itself does not appear under strain.

projects.name: orbit-map
projects.what_it_does: Maps conceptual gravity across indexed artifacts by showing tag centers, clusters, and connection strength in a text-first way.
notes: A coherent diagnostic/visual project with foundry-native shape.
Interesting, but not currently under strong practical pressure compared with continuity infrastructure.
next_actions: Leave it quiet unless a real review need appears for conceptual topology or archive navigation.
If revisited, keep it text-first rather than drifting toward a graph UI.
signals: Fits the diagnostic/visual track, but not the current center of gravity.

projects.name: foundry-registry
projects.what_it_does: Keeps a hand-editable registry of foundry projects and prints terminal summaries, detail views, and coverage validation for the machine room.
notes: This is now a live machine-room surface rather than just a seeded inventory file.
Its value comes from staying simple enough to trust and edit by hand.
It should reflect settled decisions and current pressure, not pretend to be automation.
next_actions: Refresh the registry after meaningful implementation, review, or doctrine shifts so it stays believable.
Keep the CLI narrow; do not turn this into a project management layer.
signals: Validation should stay green as new project directories appear.
The registry now includes drift-review and reflects the late-2026-03-10 machine-room state.

projects.name: foundry-planner
projects.what_it_does: Keeps a hand-editable planning surface for current goals, blockers, requests, testing pressure, and future project lines in the machine room.
dependencies: plan.json under its own project directory
notes: This complements the registry by answering what should happen next rather than what exists.
It is intentionally not generic project-management software.
next_actions: Keep the planner coherent with registry reality after meaningful project changes.
signals: Validation expects current project-directory coverage.

projects.name: intake-triage
projects.what_it_does: Reads manual intake items and emits a structured local triage review surface with disposition, urgency, confidence, and rationale.
notes: A bounded review utility that preserves ambiguity rather than overclaiming.
It should remain local and inspectable.
next_actions: Leave it quiet unless real intake review exposes a concrete gap.
signals: The heuristic surface is intentionally readable and modest.

projects.name: situation-board
projects.what_it_does: Builds a compact markdown board from manually maintained situation notes so current attention, follow-up, and hold state stay legible.
notes: This is a manual situational-awareness surface, not a dashboard or notification system.
Its value comes from declared inputs staying visible.
next_actions: Keep it modest and file-driven.
signals: The generated board reflects declared inputs only.

projects.name: transcript-review-note-generator
projects.what_it_does: Turns one plain-text transcript into a markdown review note with decisions, open threads, project ideas, candidate memory promotions, artifact candidates, and residue.
notes: It is a local review bridge rather than a generic summarizer.
Residue is treated as first-class output instead of being silently discarded.
next_actions: Use it on real transcripts before widening the heuristic surface.
signals: The tool suggests destination layers without auto-writing memory or projects.

projects.name: reading-library
projects.what_it_does: Keeps a hand-editable local library of reading items and surfaces active or returning reading pressure tied to current themes and projects.
notes: This is intentionally a pressure surface rather than a completion tracker.
One file per item keeps the library inspectable and artifact-like without adding more infrastructure.
The first seeded set is tied to continuity, correspondence, recurrence, relationship boundaries, and small systems with soul.
next_actions: Use it in real machine-room reading flow and see whether item notes or by-theme/by-project views want to be the next bounded slice.
Keep recurrence support light; do not let it turn into reading metrics or quote-hoarding.
signals: The active surface intentionally includes high-pressure paused items so important sources do not disappear when they leave the desk.
Returning sources are tracked through explicit return markers rather than hidden scoring.

projects.name: correspondence-archive
projects.what_it_does: Holds addressed thought over time as durable correspondence artifacts, preserving exchange, threading, chronology, and unresolved pressure.
notes: This is Phase A's lead project—opening genuinely new territory while staying adjacent to current work.
One markdown file per item preserves artifact quality and makes correspondence feel like a drawer of letters rather than database records.
The system is intentionally local-first and text-first with no send mechanism—it preserves addressed exchange as archive, not as transmission protocol.
Success depends on whether it feels distinct from notes and chat while creating useful thread/unresolved views.
next_actions: Use it for real correspondence and see whether the current shape feels alive.
Only deepen if lived use reveals concrete missing moves—project/theme linkage, return markers, or richer thread navigation.
Keep the archival feel strong; do not let it become inbox sludge or pseudo-intimacy infrastructure.
signals: This addresses the missing layer identified in Phase A planning: durable addressed exchange that is neither prompt scroll nor public essay.
The v1 scope is deliberately bounded—smallest coherent implementation that tests whether correspondence deserves its own room.

projects.name: field-notes
projects.what_it_does: Keeps a local archive of field notes as individual artifacts, with recent, returning, and by-tag views for lived observation and subtle recurring texture.
notes: This gives overheard lines, social weather, scenes, motifs, and charged fragments their own room rather than flattening them into notes or projects.
One markdown file per note preserves artifact feel and makes chronology, ambiguity, and recurrence hand-editable.
Returning is explicit via manual return markers rather than hidden inference or mood analytics.
next_actions: Use it on real field notes and see whether the archive still feels alive after more than the seed set.
Only add deeper surfaces if lived use clearly wants one bounded move beyond recent/returning/by-tag.
Protect the project from drifting toward monitoring, journaling-by-force, or generic capture sludge.
signals: The project directly widens the archive into lived observation and atmospheric residue, pairing with the institutional-temperature memo without becoming surveillance infrastructure.
Its first bounded slice is now real: archive artifacts plus list/show/recent/returning/by-tag/template/validate.

projects.name: voice-style-workshop
projects.what_it_does: Keeps a local archive of charged style fragments, making returning lines, tonal moves, structural gestures, and source-linked pressure legible without turning style into rules.
notes: This gives sentence pressure and structural recurrence their own room rather than dissolving them into drafts, notes, or reading traces.
One markdown file per fragment preserves artifact feel and keeps judgments about aliveness, return, and caution visible by hand.
The seed set includes a deliberate anti-pattern fragment so the workshop can hold restraint as well as admiration.
next_actions: Use it on real fragments and see whether the current fragment/returning/tag/source surfaces stay alive after more than the seed set.
Only add style-note or pattern surfaces after enough real fragments accumulate to justify another bounded slice.
Protect it from drifting into quote-hoarding, coaching doctrine, or scorekeeping.
signals: This is the first bounded implementation of the voice/style workshop plan: fragment archive plus returning, by-tag, and by-source views.
It directly applies the small-systems-with-soul stance by staying local, inspectable, constrained, textured, and human-scale.
